title: Release Sentinel: Guided Traffic Split & Emergency Snapback Flow
creator: Asha Kumar
description:
Problem statement:
Teams deploying model variants need a single guided flow to configure gradual traffic shifts, surface safety and cost guardrails, and execute an emergency snapback without digging into infra. Current console patterns are fragmented between a traffic-split editor, raw routing JSON, and an observability page; customers ask for a concise, auditable path that makes trade-offs explicit and reduces accidental exposure during ramps.

Scope and goals:
- Design a ‘Release Sentinel’ flow in Console that guides PMs/Engineers through: hypothesis, traffic schedule, risk gates (latency/error/quality thresholds), cost budget limits, and an emergency snapback action.
- Provide explainable defaults and a single-click emergency revert that preserves telemetry context (who triggered, why, time).
- Surface estimated cost delta and latency impact for each split step in the planner.
- Ensure the flow ties to existing rollout artifacts: canary groups, evaluation prompt sets, and rollout audit logs.

Deliverables:
- Low-fi flows for planner, guardrail editor, and snapback confirmation modal.
- Mid-fi Figma prototypes for accessibility run and microcopy.
- Usability test script + task list for 6 internal users and 4 external PMs.
- Handoff notes to ENG for API contract (expected fields) and Acceptance Criteria.

Success metrics:
- Usability test: task completion >= 90% for creating a scheduled split with guardrails.
- Time to execute emergency snapback < 30s (measured in mock environment).
- Reduction in support escalations for routing mistakes by 40% in first quarter after launch.

Constraints & assumptions:
- Must integrate with existing rollout audit log model and Console RBAC (no new auth surface).
- Cost estimates are approximate and derived from token-rate and historical throughput; accuracy target +/- 15%.
- Emergency snapback should not require infra changes; implement as atomic routing overwrite with rollback metadata.

Audience:
- Primary: Platform/Product engineers, Release managers, SRE on-call.
- Secondary: PMs and non-technical stakeholders who monitor rollouts.
